newsitem.title: CROATIA: Mission launched to trace missing in ex-Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Mission launched to trace missing in ex-Yugoslavia.

text.p: International human rights officials began a week-long mission to former Yugoslavia on Monday to raise the issue of missing persons with leaders of Croatia, Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.
The recently-formed International Commission for Missing Persons (ICMP), headed by former U.S. Secretary of State Cyrus Vance, kicked off the tour by meeting Croatian president Franjo Tudjman.
"We want to meet all governmental leaders on this critical issue," Vance told reporters after meeting an association of Croatian mothers of the disappeared.
Some 19,200 people are still unaccounted for in Croatia and Bosnia, where wars followed their secession from federal Yugoslavia in 1991 and 1992 respectively.

The ICMP will look into unresolved search requests, some 16,000 of them filed from Bosnia, 2,300 from Croatia and 206 from rump Yugoslavia, said Cornelio Sommaruga, head of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).
Another 717 pending cases were raised by minority Croatian Serbs, who fled en masse from their breakway enclaves ahead of Croatian army offensives last year.

Vance said the ICPM would try to pressure governments which did not comply. Jose Ayallo Lasso, U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights, said the group would "work through persuasion. We'll be raising the issue of moral commitment".
"It's the duty of the parties involved to cooperate without carrots. There are rules out there to give information, which they very well know," said Herbert Okun, former U.S. ambassador to the U.N.

The group is scheduled to visit Sarajevo, Belgrade, the Bosnian Serb stronghold of Banja Luka and the Croatian town of Vukovar, from which some 1,100 people are still unaccounted for after it was captured by rebel Serb troops in November 1991.
